explanations.Explain how the written row satisfies pr: Constraint: migration control/priv/repo/migrations/20260904010000_complete_engineering_workspace.exs:18-19 creates `project_resources_sync_status_check` as `sync_status IN ('unknown','syncing','synced','stale','failed')`, so "stale" is an admitted value at the database level (the migration tree is untouched by the change). The schema mirrors this: ProjectResource @sync_statuses (control/lib/symmetry_control/workspaces/schemas.ex:105) contains "stale", sync_changeset -> validate_resource applies validate_inclusion(:sync_status, @sync_statuses) and check_constraint(:sync_status, name: :project_resources_sync_status_check) (schemas.ex:219, 226), so an inadmissible value would surface as a changeset error instead of a raised constraint violation. Attention-message validation: the same validate_resource pipeline runs validate_attention_message/1 (schemas.ex:258-269), which requires a non-blank status_message whenever status is "degraded"/"offline" or sync_status is "stale"/"failed"; the new write path always supplies the classified message ("Provider resource was not found" for :not_found) together with status "degraded", so the intended row is simultaneously admitted by the DB constraint and by the attention-message rule - and the focused test's re-read `Repo.get!(ProjectResource, resource.id)` (test file lines 94-100 and 129-135) proves the row was actually committed, not just returned in memory. Concurrency: record_resource_failure/3 wraps the write in Repo.transaction that first locks the Project FOR SHARE and then the ProjectResource FOR UPDATE (integrations.ex:1591-1604, matching the documented global lock order in docs/design/data.md:340-343), and admits the write only after `matches_version(resource, resource_snapshot.lock_version)` (implemented at integrations.ex:1886-1887) and after the changeset's optimistic_lock(:lock_version) plus stale-aware Repo.update (update_with_stale_error/1, integrations.ex:1889-1892). The snapshot lock_version was read before the provider call, so any concurrent writer that committed a newer revision makes the guard fail with {:error, :stale}; the transaction returns the bare :stale atom, the outer case maps it to {:error, :stale}, and no update is issued in that branch, so the newer row remains authoritative. The third scenario of the new test exercises exactly that interleaving against real code (deferred provider response held by a Task and released only after Workspaces.update_resource bumps lock_version), asserting {:error, :stale} and an intact newer row (external_ref rebound, status/sync_status "unknown", status_message nil, last_checked_at nil); the traced focused-tests run recorded in checks/attempt-0001 ran all three tests on this exact Subject (subject_hash_before == subject_hash_after == sha256:5c8b1a80..., exit 0, "Result: 3 passed") and the full suite plus both e2e gates passed on the same hash, which independently corroborates that neither the constraint, the attention validation, nor the stale-write guard was weakened.
explanations.Explain why a definite provider identity: Both required entry points converge on one failure writer. Integrations.sync_resource/1 (control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:270-275) and Integrations.sync_all_resources/0 (integrations.ex:252-265, which maps every active project resource through sync_resource/1) call sync_connected_resource/1 (integrations.ex:660-679); its else branch routes any non-nil, non-:stale, non-:state_conflict provider error to `record_resource_failure(resource, reason)` (line 676) and the not-connected case to `record_resource_failure(resource, :not_connected)` (line 677). record_resource_failure/2 (1582-1585) is only a classifier: it calls the unchanged `failure/1`, where `failure({:http, 404, _body})` yields `{:not_found, "Provider resource was not found"}` (line 1642) - the same shape the real providers emit (`{:error, {:http, status, body}}`, e.g. providers/github.ex:951 and providers/azure_devops.ex:868). record_resource_failure/3 (1587-1630) is therefore the code path that decides the persisted sync_status: it computes `sync_status = failure_sync_status(code)` once, then inside a Repo.transaction writes the row through ProjectResource.sync_changeset with status "degraded", that sync_status, the classified status_message and a fresh last_checked_at, and finally returns the original `code` unchanged as `{:error, code, degraded}`. The only added logic is the private failure_sync_status/1 (1631-1636): `failure_sync_status(:not_found) -> "stale"`, any other code -> "failed". Because the code is produced by the untouched failure/1, the requirement holds by construction: :not_found (definite provider identity loss, HTTP 404) persists stale, while transport (:provider_failure, "Provider transport failed"), unauthorized (:provider_unauthorized, "Provider authentication failed"), forbidden 403 and capability (:forbidden, "Provider permission denied"/"Connection capability is not granted"), invalid response (:provider_failure, "Provider response is invalid") and not connected (:not_connected, "Resource has no external connection") still persist "failed" - all six classifications and their exact caller-visible codes/messages are pinned by the second test ("a transient provider failure keeps persisting failed synchronization", integrations.ex is the only production file changed: git diff HEAD shows a single hunk pair, 10 insertions/1 deletion, no change to failure/1).

findings.description: The new decision point `failure_sync_status/1` (control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations.ex:1631-1636) is consulted by every `record_resource_failure/3` call, so the :not_found classification now persists sync_status "stale" for provider *action* failure projections too, not only for the two synchronization entry points named in the outcome: `SymmetryControl.Integrations.project_provider_action_failure/2` (integrations.ex:538-548, reached from control/lib/symmetry_control/integrations/provider_access.ex:2201 with {:provider_action_failure, :not_found, :definite, message}) and `record_provider_action_failure/3` (integrations.ex:1132-1152) when the provider action error classifies as :not_found via `provider_action_error/1`/`failure/1`. Reviewed and accepted as a semantically consistent consequence of the required rule (definite provider identity loss => stale): failure/1 and `provider_action_error/1` codes are untouched, the returned error codes for callers are unchanged, no constraint/authority/gate is affected, "stale" is already an admissible sync_status, and no existing test asserted "failed" for a 404 provider action (no 404 provider result exists in control/test/symmetry_control/integrations_test.exs; full-suite = 854 passed / 21 skipped, provider-broker-e2e = 4 passed). No fix required; flagged so the widened blast radius is on record.

In the third test the closing assertion `stale_model.health.synchronization == "attention"` (control/test/symmetry_control/resource_sync_identity_loss_test.exs:283) is not by itself discriminating: ReadModel.synchronization_health/1 (control/lib/symmetry_control/workspaces/read_model.ex:540-553) maps both "failed" and "stale" to "attention", so that line would also hold under the old behaviour. Discrimination for the requirement is carried by the immediately preceding assertions in the same test (lines 272-279) and by test one (lines 88-100, 116-135), which pin the returned struct and the re-read database row to sync_status "stale" with the exact message "Provider resource was not found"; a grep of control/lib shows the new `failure_sync_status(:not_found)` clause is the only writer of resource sync_status "stale" (the other "stale" hits are goals.ex:2475 and provider_access.ex:2362, unrelated), so those assertions cannot pass unless the change is present. Tests remain non-vacuous; no change required.

No defect and no action required.
